title: Dictionaries and key lookup
subtitle: A dictionary associates keys with values so you can look up a value by name.
concept: A dictionary associates keys with values so you can look up a value by name.
intuition: An address book finds a phone number by name, without needing its position.
objectives: Choose a default for a missing key

body.title: Write a price table
body.text: prices = {"apple": 3, "bread": 5} is a dictionary. Each pair has a key on the left and its value on the right. A colon joins them; commas separate pairs. prices["apple"] retrieves 3 by key. These square brackets contain a key, not a list position.

body.title: Add and update by key
body.text: prices["milk"] = 4 adds a new product; prices["apple"] = 6 updates an existing price. Each key has one current value. for name in prices: visits the keys; prices[name] retrieves the corresponding value.

body.title: Choose a default for a missing key
body.text: Indexing a missing key raises KeyError. prices.get("rice", 0) retrieves the value if present and returns 0 otherwise, without inserting rice. This is useful for counting: counts[name] = counts.get(name, 0) + 1 starts an unseen item at 0 and adds one.

formalDefinition.text: A dictionary maps keys to values. Square brackets read an existing key; get can supply a default for a missing key.
conditions: A key must exist for direct indexed lookup. For a missing key, get lets you choose a default.

derivation.text: Assigning the same key again changes its value to 6.
It does not create a second apple key.

workedExamples.title: Find a price by product name
workedExamples.problem: Look up apple, then change its price.
steps: Assigning the same key again changes its value to 6.
It does not create a second apple key.

workedExamples.title: Count each fruit
workedExamples.problem: Count occurrences in apple, pear, apple.
steps: For a new fruit, get returns 0.
Add 1 and store it under the same key.
On the second apple, update its count from 1 to 2.

commonMistakes.claim: [0] always reads the first dictionary value.
commonMistakes.correction: A dictionary uses keys. Lookup with 0 works only if 0 is an actual key.

commonMistakes.claim: get inserts a missing key automatically.
commonMistakes.correction: get only reads and returns the default; it does not insert a key.

practice.hint: Use the product name as the key.
Assign a new value to the same key.
solution: The new price replaces the old one.

practice.problem: Return 0 for rice, which has no entry.
practice.hint: Use the second argument of get.
solution: A missing key returns the default 0.

practice.problem: Count fruits from an empty list. How many keys result?
practice.hint: An empty list runs no loop iterations.
solution: The dictionary stays empty, with length 0.

learningCheck.question: prices has no rice key. Which expression returns a default of 0?
learningCheck.explanation: get supplies a default for a missing key.
feedback: Directly reading a missing key raises an exception.
Yes. A missing key returns the second argument, 0.
Dictionaries use keys. The key 0 does not mean the first position.
